Meet the author

Harni
Muharami

NHS nurse · Clinical educator · Author

Care is at the heart of my work.
And at the heart of my writing.

Based in London, I write about nursing, professional growth and the everyday work of caring for ourselves and others.

Discover my story ↓

My professional background

Experience that
informs every page.

My career has taken me from non-clinical roles to ward nursing, the emergency department and clinical education.

Working across these settings has shaped how I understand care: the decisions made under pressure, the relationships within a team and the support people need to do their work well.

Today, I lead a health training hub, supporting workforce education and practice improvement. Mentoring nurses and helping colleagues develop their careers remain central to my work.

Education
Bachelor of Science
MSc in Management and Leadership in Health
Continuing development
Currently undertaking PhD studies

Why I write

Practical insight.
A human perspective.

My books make space for both the practical and personal sides of nursing. They explore safe care, speaking up, career development and the emotional demands of working in healthcare.

I write for students finding their feet, nurses building confidence and colleagues supporting others. Beyond healthcare, my books on gratitude and relationships invite readers to reflect on their own everyday lives.

Each book has a clear audience and focus, so you can choose the one that fits your interests and stage of life.

A little more information

Before you turn the page.

Where can I buy the books?

On Amazon.co.uk, as a Kindle ebook or a paperback. harni.uk does not sell books or take payment: every buy button opens the book’s Amazon page in a new tab. All 13 books are also in Kindle Unlimited, subject to Amazon’s terms.

Who are the books written for?

Most are written for NHS nurses and other UK healthcare professionals, from students and newly qualified nurses to ward leaders. Two books, Gratitude Reimagined and The 30-Day Relationship Reboot, are for anyone. Each book page has a “Who it’s for” section.

Are the books medical advice?

No. They offer general guidance and reflection, not individual clinical, medical or legal advice, and they are not official NHS guidance. Always use current authoritative guidance, your local policies and your own professional judgement.

Do you speak at events or run sessions?

Event details are listed on the Events page when they are confirmed. If you are planning a book discussion, a nursing community event or an education session, you are welcome to send an outline through the contact page. An enquiry is not a booking.

Readers & organisers

Let’s start a conversation.

For book enquiries, reader feedback or an invitation to discuss an event, I’d be pleased to hear from you.

Author biography for organisers and press

Harni Muharami is an NHS nurse and clinical educator in London. She leads a health training hub and holds an MSc in Management and Leadership in Health. She is currently doing a PhD.
